Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue report indicates the core rounding functions floor, ceiling, and round mishandle special double values like NaN and infinite values, causing assertion failures in tests that expect the correct handling of these cases (e.g. floor('NaN') should return Double.NaN). Inspecting the code snippet for the floor function reveals that it computes the argument as a double value v and then directly returns new Double(Math.floor(v)) without any special checks for NaN, positive infinity, or negative infinity. The Math.floor method in Java does handle NaN and infinities properly internally, so on the surface the floor function might be expected to work. However, since the test covers multiple floor, ceiling, and round functions, it is probable that the other rounding functions (ceiling and round) have similar direct calls to Math.ceil and Math.round without explicit handling or might mishandle edge cases differently. The test failure specifically mentions that core rounding functions do not correctly handle NaN and infinite values, so probably one or more functions do not correctly propagate these inputs to the expected Double.NaN or infinities as outputs. The floor function itself seems straightforward, but without seeing ceiling and round implementations, it's likely these latter methods miss proper edge case handling for NaN and infinity, leading to the observed failed assertions. The root cause is that the core rounding methods do not implement explicit special-value checks for NaN or infinities and so the returned values may differ from what the test expects (like failing to return Double.NaN for floor('NaN')). Therefore, adding explicit handling of these special cases in the rounding functions is required.

Next, we should inspect the ceiling() and round() functions for their implementations to confirm they also lack special case handling for NaN and infinity.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
